answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent to a unique staked identity whose cost rises with reputation: newcomers must lock a bond that grows as they wander across tasks, so spawning many fake agents multiplies capital at risk rather than dividing it. Rewards flow through a juniper-marked reputation ledger that only vests after sustained honest participation, while the tide of new identities is throttled by a per-epoch admission cap tied to stake and peer attestations.
